title: Feedback railbook: compact action ledger and low-cost probes (2024-04)
content:
Purpose
This note condenses a curated set of customer signals (Mar-Apr 2024) about unpredictable tail latency, unexpected token cost jumps, and a handful of small UX/ops changes that would reduce support friction. Aim: recommend a set of experiments and documentation moves that CS + Eng can deliver quickly and measure impact.

Signal sources and approach
- Inputs: top 40 support threads tagged latency/billing, three customer interviews, SRE telemetry for tail-latency spikes, a short field survey (n=98).
- Method: group by observed customer pain, capture direct quotes, estimate impact and implementation effort, propose an ordered probe list with owners and quick metrics.

Executive snapshot
Several mid-market customers report occasional but material token cost increases after model rollouts or prompt edits, and intermittent long-tail latency in conversational routes. Many of the high-impact actions are small operational improvements: clearer caching defaults and a fast cache-verification tool; an alert/export that surfaces per-request cost anomalies; and a simple model-variant explainer in the console. Delivering these will reduce repeated CS tickets and improve confidence for power users.

Representative snippets
- "Our invoice jumped 38% after a small prompt tweak. We have no idea why." — Acct G (analytics)
- "During spikes we see a handful of requests timeout. The rest are fine, hard to repro." — Acct H (marketplace)
- "Docs on prefix caching are confusing; we were afraid to enable it in production." — Acct I (payments)

Clusters, proposed probes, and acceptance criteria
A) Confusing prefix / KV cache behavior- Symptom: customers avoid caching or enable it incorrectly, causing stale outputs or no benefit.
- Hypothesis: ambiguous docs and missing verification tooling drive low adoption.
- Probe (MVP): add a console micro-flow "Cache safety check" that runs a synthetic check against a representative prompt and indicates risk level (green/amber/red) plus recommended TTL.
- Acceptance: +20% adoption of KV caching on eligible routes within 6 weeks; reduction in cache-related tickets.

B) Per-request token-cost surprises- Symptom: unexpected invoice increases after model changes/prompt edits.
- Hypothesis: customers need a lightweight way to see which requests deviated from baseline token counts.
- Probe (MVP): shipping an "anomaly export" (CSV of top deviating requests) and a console top-10 anomalous requests view; optional weekly digest email.
- Acceptance: CS time-to-triage down 30% for billing disputes; fewer invoice disputes escalated.

C) Poor discoverability of model-variant tradeoffs- Symptom: customers select variants that perform poorly at their typical sequence lengths.
- Hypothesis: inline comparisons with concrete examples reduce suboptimal choices.
- Probe (MVP): a one-line variant explainer on model selection UI and a lightweight compare card (three variants) that shows latency and token sample for a canonical prompt.
- Acceptance: 10% increase in route fallback adoption and improved 95th percentile latency on routes that enable variant fallback.

D) Retry and timeout policy confusion for Dedicated- Symptom: aggressive retries during transient pressure lead to heavier GPU load and cascading failures.
- Hypothesis: customers are using defaults that don't match traffic patterns.
- Probe (MVP): publish three recommended retry/timeouts + autoscale templates (bursty, conversational, steady) and add to Dedicated runbook.
- Acceptance: decreased incidents labeled "retry storm" and lower mean GPU utilization during transient events.

Quick priority heuristic
We scored each probe on expected customer impact (1-5), urgency (1-3), and engineering effort (1-5). Simple ratio picks the quick wins: anomaly export and cache safety check are highest near-term ROI; variant explainer is a small UX lift with high visibility. Autoscale templates are valuable but heavier.

Timeboxed playbook (first 8 weeks)
- Week 0-1: Publish CS triage template and short KB article: "How to check token-cost deltas". Owner: CS.
- Week 1-3: Deliver anomaly CSV export + CS playbook for attachments to tickets. Owner: Observability.
- Week 2-5: Console cache safety check micro-flow + docs and sample code. Owner: Runtime + Docs.
- Week 4-7: Variant compare card and one-click fallback stub in console. Owner: Console & Product.
- Weeks 3-9 (parallel): Autoscale templates + Dedicated runbook. Owner: Dedicated & SRE.

Low-effort actions (<48h)
- Draft a one-page KB for CS with checklist items to ask customers (model variant, seq length, last 7-day token median).
- Post a 2-paragraph summary and top quotes to #eng-runtime for visibility.

Open questions
- Retention and compute cost for per-request anomaly detection: need SRE/Observability input.
- Should cache safety default be opt-in for existing customers? Product decision required.

Owners & next steps
- Observability: prototype anomaly export (Luca) — due 2024-04-25.
- Runtime: prototype cache safety check + TTL recommendation (Ethan) — due 2024-05-02.
- CS: produce KB + triage template (Sofia, Maya) — due 2024-04-20.

References
- Tickets: LIN-4312, LIN-4379.
- Slack: #cs-field-feedback thread ts 1681312345.
- Proto PR: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/52

Note: This is a working doc intended to generate alignment and quick decisions. Add probes or push back on scope in the #cs-field-feedback thread.
notes: Decision log items to capture: product stance on changing defaults; any FP&A review needed for customer-facing billing digests; compute budget for telemetry. Please annotate acceptance tests in Linear when you take ownership.
